historical_references.reference: Nandikaa is a Hindu name derived from the Sanskrit word 'Nandana', meaning 'delight' or 'joy'. It is believed that the name originated from the legend of Lord Shiva and his wife Parvati. According to the story, Parvati, who was the goddess of love and fertility, longed for a child. Lord Shiva, who was oblivious to her desire, was meditating deep in the forest of Kailash. Parvati, in her frustration, created a child named Ganesha from the sap of the sacred Parvata mountain. When Lord Shiva returned and found the child, he was pleased with him and named him 'Ganesha' or 'Lord of the Ganas'. Later, when Parvati gave birth to a son, she named him Nandi, which means 'joy' or 'delight', and the name eventually evolved into Nandikaa for females.

Another reference for the name Nandikaa is found in the ancient Indian epic, Mahabharata. In this epic, Nandikaa is the name of a character, the mother of Bhima, the strongest of the five Pandava brothers. Bhima was known for his extraordinary strength and was an integral part of the battle between the Pandavas and the Kauravas, which eventually led to the establishment of righteous rule. Nandikaa, being the mother of such a strong and powerful son, holds a significant place in Hindu mythology.
